newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan monopoly buys stake in Emirates Crescent.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan monopoly buys stake in Emirates Crescent.

text.p: Taiwan state oil monopoly Chinese Petroleum Corp said on Tuesday it had bought a US$75 million stake in Crescent Petroleum Co International Ltd of the United Arab Emirates.
The acquisition gives Chinese Petroleum access to 54 million barrels of oil reserves controlled by Crescent and to 14,000 barrels a day of Crescent's maximum daily production of 60,000 barrels.
Chinese Petroleum declined give a percentage for how much control of Crescent the Taiwan monopoly would have after the acquisition.
Taiwan industry sources said Chinese Petroleum would hold 40 percent of the private oil firm based in Sharjah in the United Arab Emirates.

Chinese Petroleum, Taiwan's sole crude importer, has aggressively been seeking to buy control of overseas reserves to better ensure supplies to the island's energy-hungry export manufacturing economy.
"Chinese Petroleum is actively seeking to acquire companies with rich oil holdings," the buyer said in a statement.
"From our point of view, the Middle East is an important strategic location so we are pleased to establish this cooperation relationship with Crescent Ltd."
Chinese Petroleum's move to take a stake in Crescent was sealed in a contract signing on Tuesday.

Crescent had said on February 10 that it was in talks with Chinese Petroleum but also with other suitors in South Korea, Europe and Canada. It was not immediately clear whether other Crescent stakes were transferred.
Crescent has oil and gas-producing assets in the Gulf and interests in a Pakistani refinery project and a planned gas to transport and sell gas from Qatar to Pakistan.
